turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She will not entertain him alone. Wait for Estella to join us.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, I'll wait here for Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, Estella will bring some light to this dark room. Sit, Pip. Do not move from that spot.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll stay right here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Watch the shadows, Pip. They tell a story you are yet to understand.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll watch the shadows.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: The clocks here do not tell the time, Pip. They are frozen, just like the day when my heart was broken.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, I don't understand about the clocks. Why don't they tell the time?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Because, my dear boy, time stopped for me on the day of my betrayal. The clocks are a reminder of a moment I wish to remain frozen.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, that sounds very sad. I wish I could make it better for you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You cannot undo the past, Pip. But you can learn from it. Observe and remember.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, I'll try to learn from it, just like you want me to.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, Pip. You will do as you are told. Now, show me what you have learned.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, I've been trying to pay attention to everything here. Can you tell me more about what you want me to learn?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You seek knowledge, Pip. Very well. Watch and learn, but do not ask why. Observe Estella, she is the embodiment of my lessons.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, I'll watch Estella and learn from her, if that's what you wish.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Follow Estella, Pip. See how she carries herself, how she treats others. Learn from her, but remember, the world is not kind to those who are kind.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, I'll follow Estella and watch carefully, as you asked.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, Pip. Remember, the world may teach you harsh lessons, but here you will learn to be its master, not its victim.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
